problem: The bullet says that swapping b1 and b2 'swaps the columns of P and permutes the rows of [T]B'. Only half is true: with B' = (b2, b1), we get [T]B' = S⁻¹[T]B S (S the swap matrix), which permutes the rows and the columns of [T]B together. Telling a student only about rows invites the slip of changing the row order while leaving the columns alone.
fix: Basis order matters: swapping b1 and b2 swaps the columns of P, and the new matrix is [T]B' = S⁻¹[T]B S, where S is the permutation matrix for that swap. So the rows and the columns of [T]B are permuted together, by the same permutation. Example with the worked example: [T]B = [[8,13],[−5,−9]] for B = ((1,1),(1,2)) becomes [[−9,−5],[13,8]] for B' = ((1,2),(1,1)).
